working_title: Why Is the Periodic Table in This Order?
house: STUDIO_PLAYBOOK.md §5 · re-timed from VO v04 KEEP
always_fails: fake or garbled element tiles / signs
unfinished Explorer hair or melted face
ATOMOS or SEE <film> text labels in plate
notes: Re-timed from VO v04. Board split 27 Sep for picture-change every 4–6 s (no hold >~6 s). t_s is PART-LOCAL (0 = Part 02 VO start / film 1:10). mint:true after Part 01 v05 PASS. Explorer once: 16_explorer_te_before_i.
title: The Table That Broke Its Own Rule

chapter_card.text: The Table That Broke Its Own Rule

set_language: TWO sets: Manchester 1808 schoolroom (Dalton, wooden balls, balance); St Petersburg 1869 desk (element cards, Mendeleev). Say 'same 1808 schoolroom set' / 'same 1869 card desk set'. Never 'same DNA'.
continuity_lock: Picture change every ~4–6 s. Explorer once only on the Te-before-I card swap. Readable faces for Dalton and Mendeleev. Real element symbols only (H O Au Te I Co Ni Cl Br) — never garbled tiles.
explorer_lock: Exactly ONE Explorer plate: 16_explorer_te_before_i. On model — round gold glasses, teal coat, finished hair. Attach 01_Character/05_Generation-References/hos-explorer-reference-v01.jpg.
forbidden: HARD REJECT: Orbit robot; photoreal; Ken Burns or still push; gore; lava drip / molten bead; underside lamp bulb or shade cup; unfinished flat cards; garbled/fake element letters; unfinished Explorer hair; DNA helix; ATOMOS or SEE labels; twin Explorer; never say 'same DNA' or 'lab DNA' in a Veo prompt. No Explorer except plate 16.
motion_lock: Real Veo motion every plate. No freeze-pad.
quality_note: Quality only if a plate is clearly glowing/emissive (final table glow). Fast for schoolroom, card sorts, Explorer swap without lamp glow.
board_split_2026_09_27: Split long holds from prior 10-plate board (02/03/05/06/07/10) into 20 plates ≤~5.7 s each.

plates.vo_land: Manchester, eighteen-oh-eight. A schoolteacher named John Dalton puts the old idea to work.
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Manchester 1808 schoolroom. John Dalton (readable finished face, period coat) sets wooden balls of different sizes onto a brass balance. Continuous place-on-balance motion. Silent. No Explorer. No text labels in plate. HARD REJECT: Orbit, unfinished face, garbled cards, ATOMOS.
plates.prompt_try2: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. ECU: Dalton's hands place graded wooden balls on the balance pans — face soft in background. Same 1808 schoolroom. Continuous place. Silent. No Explorer. HARD REJECT: Orbit, garbled text.

plates.vo_land: His atomic theory says every element is made of its own kind of atom,
plates.prompt: Same 1808 schoolroom set. Wooden balls of distinct sizes sit as different kinds of atoms on the desk. Continuous soft push along the row. Silent. No Explorer. HARD REJECT: Orbit, DNA helix, garbled letters.
plates.prompt_try2: Same 1808 set. Wider desk: three clearly different wooden-ball sizes as three element kinds. Continuous camera drift. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, Explorer.

plates.vo_land: and each kind has its own weight. Hydrogen is the lightest. Oxygen is heavier.
plates.prompt: Same 1808 schoolroom set. Wooden balls lined light-to-heavy: tiny light ball (hydrogen feel) then larger (oxygen feel). Continuous line-up. Silent. Real feel only — no fake tile letters. HARD REJECT: Orbit, Explorer, garbled H/O tiles.
plates.prompt_try2: Same 1808 set. Balance tips slightly as a heavier wooden ball replaces a light one. Continuous tip. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, garbled signs.

plates.vo_land: Gold is heavier still.
plates.prompt: Same 1808 schoolroom set. A dense gold-coloured wooden ball is clearly the heaviest in the line; camera settles on it. Continuous settle. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, Explorer, lava drip.
plates.prompt_try2: Same 1808 set. ECU gold-coloured heavy ball on the balance — pan sinks. Continuous sink. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit.

plates.vo_land: Why believe him? Because elements always combine in the same fixed amounts.
plates.prompt: Same 1808 set. Two kinds of wooden balls repeatedly snap together in the same count. Continuous snap-combine. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, photoreal chemistry lab, Explorer.
plates.prompt_try2: Same 1808 set. Overhead: pairs of balls always land in matching groups. Continuous land. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit.

plates.vo_land: Water is always the same mix of hydrogen and oxygen,
plates.prompt: Same 1808 set. A clear water droplet graphic resolves into two light balls and one heavier ball in a fixed ratio, then recombines to water. Continuous split/recombine. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, photoreal lab glassware hero, Explorer.
plates.prompt_try2: Same 1808 set. Wooden balls labelled only by size (not letters) form water's fixed mix on the desk. Continuous form. Silent. HARD REJECT: garbled letters, Orbit.

plates.vo_land: however you make it.
plates.prompt: Same 1808 set. Different paths (pour / heat / cool) all resolve to the same ball ratio for water. Continuous converge. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, Explorer.
plates.prompt_try2: Same 1808 set. Three paths meet at one matching ball cluster. Continuous meet. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit.

plates.vo_land: Now chemists had a ruler. Compare the weights of the atoms and line them up.
plates.prompt: Same 1808 set evolving to a simple weight ruler: wooden balls lined by mass along a wooden rule. Continuous line-up. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, Explorer, garbled scale numbers as hero.
plates.prompt_try2: Same 1808 set. Balls slide into mass order along a straight rule. Continuous slide. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit.

plates.vo_land: Sixty years later in Saint Petersburg, Dmitri Mendeleev does exactly that.
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. St Petersburg 1869 desk. Dmitri Mendeleev (readable finished face, beard, period frock) sits at a wooden desk with blank-then-writing element cards. Continuous write. Silent. No Explorer. HARD REJECT: Orbit, garbled cards, unfinished face.
plates.prompt_try2: Same 1869 desk. MCU Mendeleev writing on a card — finished face, warm lamp glow careful (no lava drip). Continuous write. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, Explorer, lamp lava.

plates.vo_land: He writes each element on a card and sorts the cards by weight.
plates.prompt: Same 1869 card desk set. Readable real element symbols on cards (H, Li, Be, C, O, Fe) sorted into a weight row. Continuous sort. Silent. No Explorer. HARD REJECT: Orbit, garbled fake letters, unfinished flat cards.
plates.prompt_try2: Same 1869 set. Hands sort a short row of clear symbol cards by weight. Continuous sort. Silent. HARD REJECT: garbled tiles, Orbit.

plates.vo_land: The properties repeat. Soft metals that fizz in water line up in one column.
plates.prompt: Same 1869 card desk set. Soft-metal cards line into one vertical column; a tiny water-fizz cue on the metals. Continuous column form. Silent. Readable real symbols (Li, Na, K). HARD REJECT: Orbit, Explorer, garbled cards.
plates.prompt_try2: Same 1869 set. Soft-metal column forms while a drop fizzes on a metal card. Continuous fizz. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit.

plates.vo_land: Harsh, reactive chlorine, bromine and iodine line up in another.
plates.prompt: Same 1869 card desk set. Cards with readable Cl, Br, I line up in a second column. Continuous line-up. Silent. No Explorer. HARD REJECT: Orbit, garbled letters, fake symbols.
plates.prompt_try2: Same 1869 set. ECU Cl Br I cards snap into a column. Continuous snap. Silent. HARD REJECT: garbled text.

plates.vo_land: He even leaves gaps for elements nobody has found yet.
plates.prompt: Same 1869 card desk set. Empty gap slots left in the card grid while filled cards stay put. Continuous leave-gap. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, Explorer, filling gaps with garbled letters.
plates.prompt_try2: Same 1869 set. Camera pushes on empty card slots in the grid. Continuous push. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit.

plates.vo_land: Then he prints his table and mails it to chemists across Europe.
plates.prompt: Same 1869 card desk set. Printed table sheets fold into letters that fly across a stylised map of Europe. Continuous print-then-fly. Silent. No readable body text as hero — table shapes only. HARD REJECT: Orbit, Explorer, ATOMOS, SEE labels.
plates.prompt_try2: Same 1869 set. Letters lift from the desk and arc over a Europe map. Continuous arc. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, garbled postage.

plates.vo_land: But look closer. Tellurium is heavier than iodine, so by weight tellurium should come after it.
plates.prompt: Same 1869 card desk set. Readable Te and I cards: Te card feels heavier on a tiny scale beside I. Continuous weigh compare. Silent. No Explorer yet. HARD REJECT: Orbit, garbled Te/I, Explorer this plate.
plates.prompt_try2: Same 1869 set. ECU Te card vs I card — Te side of the scale sinks. Continuous sink. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Mendeleev puts it before anyway, because that's where it behaves right.
plates.prompt: Same 1869 card desk set. Exactly ONE Explorer (young boy, messy brown hair, round gold glasses, teal long coat, tan vest, brown bow tie) picks up the Te card, checks the weight, frowns, puts Te back BEFORE the I card, then leaves frame. Continuous acting then leave. Attach Explorer reference. Silent. HARD REJECT: twins, no glasses, Orbit, Explorer parked all minute, garbled cards.
plates.prompt_try2: Same 1869 set. MCU: Explorer's hands (teal sleeves, glasses glint) place Te before I on the desk, then he steps out of frame. Continuous place-and-leave. Attach Explorer reference. Silent. HARD REJECT: twins, no glasses, Orbit.

plates.vo_land: Cobalt and nickel have the same trouble.
plates.prompt: Same 1869 set. Readable Co and Ni cards show the same swap trouble as Te/I. Continuous nudge-swap. Silent. No Explorer. HARD REJECT: Orbit, garbled cards.
plates.prompt_try2: Same 1869 set. ECU Co and Ni cards wobble as if unsure of order. Continuous wobble. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit.

plates.vo_land: Mendeleev guessed the weights had been measured wrong. They hadn't.
plates.prompt: Same 1869 set. A brass scale confirms the card weights are correct; the wrong-measurement guess fails. Continuous confirm. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, Explorer.
plates.prompt_try2: Same 1869 set. Scale stays true while a crossed-out guess chalk mark fades. Continuous fade. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit.

plates.vo_land: So the table works, but it breaks its own rule.
plates.prompt: Same 1869 set. Finished periodic table layout glows softly with warm emissive light while Te/I still feel wrong in place. Continuous soft glow pulse. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, Explorer, Ken Burns only, lamp lava drip.
plates.prompt_try2: Same 1869 set. Wider: glowing table on the wall, Te/I cards on the desk still mismatched. Continuous soft camera drift. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, lava drip.

plates.vo_land: If weight isn't the real order, what is?
plates.prompt: Same 1869 set. Open question: empty space beyond the glowing table — soft push into unresolved dark. Continuous soft push. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, Explorer, Ken Burns only, SEE labels.
plates.prompt_try2: Same 1869 set. Cards settle; camera lifts toward unanswered dark above the desk. Continuous lift. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit.
